title: The parse method returns incorrect output when both strictNullHandling and allowEmptyArrays are set to true
contractNotes: Issue states stringify/parse round-trip with strictNullHandling and allowEmptyArrays must preserve empty arrays. Cases vary field names, nested paths, encoded brackets and preserve scalar-null and nonempty-array behavior. No solution comments enter actor prompt.

title: Parsing object with array doesn't split a value
contractNotes: Issue explicitly expects comma splitting of object-form query input, just as string input. Cases vary flat/nested keys and multiple fields while preserving no-comma, comma:false, primitive values, and input immutability.

title: Globstar not matching zero
publicBody:
According to the docs, minimatch should behave like Bash 4.1.

According to this comment, the `/path/**/*.html` pattern should match `/path/to/page.html`, `/path/to/web/page.html`, and also `/path/page.html`, for Bash 4 and above. This works in my Bash 4.4.20.

However, if I use minimatch to create a RegExp for the pattern above:

```
const makeRe = require("minimatch").makeRe;
const regex = makeRe("/path/**/*.html");
```
the resulting RegExp seems to be `^(?:\/path\/(?:(?!(?:\/|^)\.).)*?\/(?!\.)(?=.)[^\/]*?\.html)$`, which although matches `/path/to/page.html` and `/path/to/web/page.html`, it doesn't match `/path/page.html`
